prompt: Two identical coaxial loops carry equal currents in opposite senses. Net B at the midpoint of their axis is:
options: Same as one loop's centre value
explain: By symmetry the two axial fields are equal and opposite at the midpoint, so they cancel.

subject: Physics
topic: Field on axis/centre of circular loop
prompt: Concentric coplanar loops of radii R and 2R carry currents I₁, I₂ in opposite senses. B = 0 at centre if I₂/I₁ =
explain: Fields cancel when I₁/R = I₂/2R, which gives I₂ = 2I₁.

subject: Physics
topic: Field on axis/centre of circular loop
prompt: In the Biot–Savart law for a circular loop's centre, why does dB from all elements add directly as scalars?
options: The dB components cancel along the axis
All dB point the same way and dl ⟂ r
explain: Each dl ⟂ r so sinθ = 1, and every dB is along the axis in the same direction.

subject: Physics
topic: Field of finite and infinite straight wire
prompt: Two long crossing insulated wires lie along +x and +y axes, each with current I outward. Net B at (a, a)?
explain: Each gives μ₀I/2πa, along +z and −z respectively, so they cancel at (a, a).

subject: Physics
prompt: Ampère's law gives B = μ₀nI for a solenoid using a loop whose inside side lies:
options: Along a circle coaxial with the solenoid
Parallel to the axis, inside the solenoid
explain: A rectangular loop has one side inside parallel to the axis. The outside side contributes zero, and the sides perpendicular to the axis give B·dl = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: A wire of length L carries current I perpendicular to B. If the current is reversed, the force magnitude and direction:
explain: F = I L × B is linear in I, so reversing I reverses F with the same magnitude.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two long parallel wires carry unequal currents in opposite directions. Net B is zero at a point:
options: Between them, nearer the larger current
Outside them, nearer the larger current
Outside them, nearer the smaller current
Between them, nearer the smaller current
explain: Between the wires the fields add. Outside, they cancel where B₁ = B₂, which is nearer the smaller current.

subject: Physics
prompt: The shunt wire of an ammeter is made thick mainly because
options: it must have a high resistance
it has to be strongly magnetic
it must be a good insulator
it carries most of the current
explain: Most of the current passes through the shunt, so a thick, low-resistance wire is needed to avoid heating.

subject: Physics
prompt: If the shunt of an ammeter gets disconnected (open) while measuring a large current, then
options: the full current flows through the galvanometer
explain: With no parallel path, the entire current passes through the coil and may burn it.

subject: Physics
prompt: A multirange ammeter obtains its different ranges by
options: using series resistors of different values
changing the number of turns online
explain: Different parallel shunts, selected by a switch, give different current ranges.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two voltmeters of ranges V₁ and V₂ are made from the same galvanometer. Ratio of their resistances?
explain: R_v = V/I_g with the same I_g, so resistance is proportional to the range.

subject: Physics
prompt: For an accurate reading, the resistance of a voltmeter should be compared with the resistance across which it is connected:
explain: A high R_V draws negligible current, so the circuit is hardly disturbed and the reading is close to the true value.

subject: Physics
prompt: A voltmeter is connected across a resistor R in a circuit. The effective resistance between those points becomes:
explain: The voltmeter is in parallel with R, so the combined resistance is less than R. This is why it reads low.

subject: Physics
prompt: The magnetic force between two long parallel current-carrying wires acts along:
options: Perpendicular to the plane of the wires
The direction of the net current
The line joining them, perpendicular to wires
explain: B of one wire is perpendicular to the plane of the wires, so F = I L×B lies in that plane, along the line joining them.

subject: Physics
prompt: Galvanometer G with shunt S in parallel: ratio of power dissipated in galvanometer to that in shunt is:
explain: Same p.d. across both, so P ∝ 1/R, giving P_g/P_s = S/G.

subject: Physics
prompt: Along the axis of a circular current loop, the field magnitude is maximum at:
explain: The denominator (R²+x²)^(3/2) is smallest at x = 0, so B is maximum there and falls off on both sides.

subject: Physics
prompt: Three-quarter circular wire of radius R carries current I. Field at its centre is:
explain: B = (θ/2π)(μ₀I/2R) with θ = 3π/2 gives 3μ₀I/8R.

subject: Physics
topic: Field on axis/centre of circular loop
prompt: Concentric coplanar loops of radii R and 2R carry equal current I in the same sense. Net B at centre:
explain: B = μ₀I/2R + μ₀I/4R = 3μ₀I/4R; same sense, so the fields add.

subject: Physics
topic: Field on axis/centre of circular loop
prompt: Current I enters a uniform circular ring at A, leaves at B (any two points). Net B at the ring's centre is:
formula: B ∝ I·l for an arc, and I₁l₁ = I₂l₂
explain: Parallel arcs have I₁l₁ = I₂l₂, so their fields at the centre are equal and opposite and cancel.

subject: Physics
topic: Field of finite and infinite straight wire
prompt: ∮B·dl along a circular arc centred on a long wire (current I), subtending angle θ at the wire:
explain: B is constant on the arc, so B·rθ = (μ₀I/2πr)·rθ = μ₀Iθ/2π.

subject: Physics
topic: Field of finite and infinite straight wire
prompt: Four long parallel wires at square corners carry equal currents, alternately in and out. B at the centre:
explain: Each diagonal pair has the same current direction, so their fields at the centre cancel.

subject: Physics
topic: Field of finite and infinite straight wire
prompt: Coaxial cable: inner conductor current I, outer −I. B between them at distance r from the axis:
explain: Amperian loop between the conductors encloses only the inner current I.

subject: Physics
topic: Field of finite and infinite straight wire
prompt: An electron moves parallel to the current direction near a long straight wire. The force on it is:
explain: Electron motion is equivalent to a current opposite to I, and antiparallel currents repel.

subject: Physics
prompt: Infinite plane sheet, uniform surface current density K. B at distance d from it is:
explain: A rectangular Amperian loop gives 2Bl = μ₀Kl, so B = μ₀K/2, uniform and independent of d.

subject: Physics
prompt: Long ideal solenoid: n and I fixed, its radius is doubled. The inner field becomes:
explain: B = μ₀nI contains no radius, so the field stays uniform and unchanged.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two parallel infinite sheets carry equal, opposite surface currents K. B between them is:
explain: Each sheet gives μ₀K/2. They add between the sheets, so B = μ₀K there, and cancel outside.

subject: Physics
prompt: A proton and an electron move with the same velocity in the same uniform B. Their magnetic forces are:
options: Equal in magnitude, opposite in direction
explain: |q| is the same, so the magnitudes are equal; the opposite sign of q reverses the direction of F.

subject: Physics
prompt: A charge is released from rest in uniform E and B fields that are parallel. It moves:
options: Along a straight line along E
explain: At rest, F_B = 0, so only qE acts. The velocity stays parallel to B, so F_B stays zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: A charge enters a wide uniform B region perpendicular to its straight edge and to B. Time spent inside is:
explain: It completes a semicircle before leaving the field, so t = T/2 = πm/(qB), independent of speed.

subject: Physics
prompt: A loosely hanging spring (slinky) carries a current through its coils. The coils:
explain: Adjacent turns carry parallel currents, which attract, so the spring contracts.

subject: Physics
prompt: The magnetic force on a current-carrying wire in B is basically the force on:
options: Moving charge carriers, passed on to the lattice
explain: Lorentz force acts on drifting carriers and is transmitted to the wire via collisions.

subject: Physics
prompt: A circular ring (radius R, current I) lies in a radial magnetic field of magnitude B at every point. Net force is:
options: 2πRIB in the plane of the ring
explain: B ⟂ current everywhere, so each element's force points along the axis. They add up to I·(2πR)·B.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two neutral wires carrying currents attract or repel mainly because of:
options: Net electrostatic charge on the wires
explain: Wires are electrically neutral, so the force is magnetic: one current moves in the other's field.

subject: Physics
prompt: A positive charge moves parallel to a long wire, in the same direction as its current. The force on it is:
explain: The moving charge acts like a parallel current element, which is attracted to the wire.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two parallel electron beams, each of speed v ≪ c, in vacuum. Magnetic force : electric force between them =
explain: F_mag/F_elec = μ₀ε₀v² = v²/c², so repulsive electric force dominates; net force is repulsive.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two coaxial circular loops placed close together carry currents in the same sense. They:
explain: Adjacent segments carry parallel currents, which attract; so the loops attract.

subject: Physics
topic: Current loop as magnetic dipole moment
prompt: Small loop of moment m: field magnitude at equatorial distance r (r ≫ size) is:
explain: The equatorial field is half the axial value and points opposite to m.

subject: Physics
topic: Current loop as magnetic dipole moment
prompt: A small current loop with m parallel to B sits in a non-uniform field. The net force pulls it toward:
explain: With m ∥ B, U = −mB falls where B is larger, so the dipole moves toward stronger field.

subject: Physics
topic: Current loop as magnetic dipole moment
prompt: A magnetic dipole m (moment of inertia J) makes small oscillations in field B. Its time period is:
explain: Restoring torque ≈ −mBθ, so ω² = mB/J, giving T = 2π√(J/mB).

subject: Physics
topic: Torque on current loop in uniform B
prompt: The product m·B (magnetic moment × field) has the same dimensions as:
explain: A·m²·T = N·m = J, which is the dimension of energy (and of torque).

subject: Physics
prompt: Besides making the field radial, the soft iron core inside the galvanometer coil also:
explain: High-permeability soft iron concentrates the flux, increasing B in the gap and hence sensitivity.

subject: Physics
prompt: Compared with the bare galvanometer, deflection per unit total current in the ammeter made with a shunt is:
explain: Only a small fraction G... S/(S+G) of the total current passes through the coil, so sensitivity falls.

subject: Physics
prompt: Coil resistance G rises on heating while the shunt S stays fixed. The ammeter reading becomes
explain: Larger G sends a smaller fraction S/(G+S) of the current through the coil, so the deflection falls.

subject: Physics

explain: The same deflection now represents n times the current, so current per division increases n times.
